title: Globalizing local towers of normalized point blowups
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $s_1,\ldots,s_r$ be distinct closed points, with $r\geq0$. Put $U=S\setminus\{s_1,\ldots,s_r\}$ and $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s_i}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For each $i$, give a finite sequence $T_{i,n_i}\to\cdots\to T_{i,0}=S_i$ of proper normalized blowups, with every center a closed point over $s_i$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A normalized blowup means the blowup at the reduced closed point followed by normalization in the function field [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-sc-normalization]. There is a global finite sequence of proper normalized blowups $S'=Z_N\to\cdots\to Z_0=S$ with centers over $\{s_1,\ldots,s_r\}$, inducing an isomorphism over $U$. For each $i$, its base change to $S_i$ is the prescribed local sequence after inserting identity morphisms, and in particular $S'\times_S S_i\cong T_{i,n_i}$ over $S_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Every point $z\in S'$ over $s_i$ corresponds under this base change to a point $t\in T_{i,n_i}$ with an isomorphism of local rings $\mathcal O_{S',z}\cong\mathcal O_{T_{i,n_i},t}$. For $r=0$, take the identity tower.

source.place: Tags 0BFV (resolve-lemma-equivalence), 0BFW (resolve-lemma-equivalence-properties), 0BFX (resolve-lemma-equivalence-fibre), and 0BFZ (resolve-lemma-equivalence-sequence-normalized-blowups); the local-ring identification is localization at a point over s_i. In 0BFZ the printed set {x_1,...,x_n} denotes the specified {s_1,...,s_n}.

proof.text: First record the local objects to which gluing will apply. Every $S_i$ is Noetherian by localization of Noetherian rings. Induct on $j$: the ordinary blowup at each nongeneric point is integral by the integral-blowup theorem, and the normalization assertion below supplies the next normal integral stage. Every $T_{i,j}\to S_i$ is proper by composition and hence has Noetherian source by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem. On each affine chart its finite-type algebra is finitely presented by the Noetherian finite-presentation lemma; properness supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Thus these are morphisms of finite presentation. For a normalized stage, apply the generic-residue-field normalization theorem with $x$ the generic point of its integral ordinary blowup and $K=\kappa(x)$ (extension degree one): its source is integral and all its local rings are integrally closed domains. The initial $S_i$ is normal because its stalks are stalks of $S$. Away from its center the ordinary blowup is an isomorphism by the blowup-complement theorem, and normalization of a normal domain adds no elements to its fraction field. Consequently every $T_{i,j}$ is normal integral and its map to $S_i$ is an isomorphism over $V_i$. No finiteness of normalization on an arbitrary Noetherian scheme is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BFV and 0BFZ, finite-presentation setting; normality from morphisms.tex, Tags 035Q and 035I, specialized at the generic point

proof.text: Here is the localization calculation used throughout. For any $X\to S$, choose $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ containing $s_i$, corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset A$, and an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ above it. The pullback chart is $\operatorname{Spec}((A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B)$. Its points correspond to primes $\mathfrak q\subset B$ whose contraction lies in $\mathfrak p$; at such a point the local ring is $((A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B)_{\mathfrak q}=B_{\mathfrak q}$, since every denominator already lies outside $\mathfrak q$. In particular the pullback gives a bijection of the points over $s_i$ and an isomorphism of their local rings. Tensoring either chart with $\kappa(s_i)$ gives the same fibre ring, so this is an isomorphism of fibres as schemes. A closed point in that fibre is closed in $X$, because the fibre over the closed point $s_i$ is closed. These chart identifications agree on overlaps by their fraction formulas.

source.place: Tag 0BFX (resolve-lemma-equivalence-fibre); the displayed fraction calculation supplies the local-ring strengthening

proof.text: Choose a total ordering of the $N=\sum_i n_i$ prescribed operations that respects the order within each local tower. After $k$ operations keep indices $a_i\leq n_i$, with $\sum_i a_i=k$, and a normal integral Noetherian scheme $Z_k$, proper and of finite presentation over $S$, identified with $U$ over $U$ and with $T_{i,a_i}$ after base change to $S_i$. Keep also the identifications of all earlier transition morphisms. For $k=0$, take $Z_0=S$, $a_i=0$, and the identity identifications. If $N=0$, this is already the desired tower, including the cases $r=0$ and all $n_i=0$. In the remaining induction $S$ has a nongeneric chosen center, so $U$ contains its generic point. In dimension zero a nonempty integral normalized blowup at the sole point cannot be supplied: the ordinary blowup of the zero ideal is empty and has no function field, so only the zero-length input occurs.

source.place: Tag 0BFZ, reduction to the point-by-point construction in Tag 0BFY (resolve-lemma-equivalence-sequence-blowups)

proof.text: Suppose the next operation is $T_{i,a_i+1}\to T_{i,a_i}$ at $t$. By Step 2 the closed point $t$ in the fibre corresponds to a closed point $z\in Z_k$ over $s_i$. Give $z$ its reduced closed subscheme structure, and blow up its ideal $\mathcal I_z$: $b:W=\operatorname{Bl}_z(Z_k)\to Z_k$. On a Noetherian affine chart this ideal is finitely generated, so the blowup-properness theorem applies. Its ideal is nonzero: if $z$ were the generic point, the corresponding local ordinary blowup would be empty, contradicting the supplied next integral normalized stage. The integral-blowup theorem therefore makes $W$ integral. Since $V(\mathcal I_z)=\{z\}$, the blowup-complement theorem makes $b$ an isomorphism over $Z_k\setminus\{z\}$. Thus $W\to S$ is proper, is an isomorphism over $U$, and is Noetherian by finite type over $S$. The same affine Noetherian finite-presentation argument as in Step 1 makes $W\to S$ finitely presented.

source.place: Tags 0BFY and 0BFZ, next point blowup; divisors.tex, Tag 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme)

proof.text: The maps $S_j\to S$ are flat: on affine charts their stalk maps are localizations, flat by the localization-flat theorem. The projection $Z_k\times_SS_j\to Z_k$ has the same localization description, hence is flat as well. Apply the flat blowup base-change theorem. For $j=i$ it identifies $W\times_SS_i$ with the ordinary blowup of $T_{i,a_i}$ at $t$; the pulled-back center is the reduced point because the point and residue-field calculation of Step 2 identifies its closed immersion. For $j\ne i$ the center pulls back to the empty subscheme: no point of $S_j$ maps to the distinct closed point $s_i$. Its ideal is the unit ideal, so $W\times_SS_j\cong T_{j,a_j}$ by the Cartier-center theorem. These identifications commute with the blowup structure maps.

source.place: Tags 0BFY and 0BFZ, base-changing the chosen point blowup; comparison defined in def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map

proof.text: Set $Y_i=T_{i,a_i+1}$ and $Y_j=T_{j,a_j}$ for $j\ne i$. They are the finite-presentation objects of Step 1. By the gluing equivalence there is a finite-presentation $S$-scheme $Z^+$, equal to $U$ over $U$, with specified isomorphisms $Z^+\times_SS_j\cong Y_j$. Apply full faithfulness to two families of arrows: the prescribed next map $Y_i\to T_{i,a_i}$ and identities elsewhere give $a:Z^+\to Z_k$; the normalization map $Y_i\to W\times_SS_i$ and identities elsewhere give $q:Z^+\to W$. Uniqueness of the lifted arrows gives $bq=a$, since this equality holds for every local arrow. Each local map of $a$ is proper (the prescribed next map or an identity), so the arrow-properness clause gives that $a$ is proper. Each local map of $q$ is integral (a normalization map or an identity), so the integral-arrow clause gives that $q$ is integral. This avoids assuming that the normalization of $W$ is finite before constructing $Z^+$.

source.place: Tags 0BFV, 0BFW, 0BFZ; limits.tex Tag 0EY3(2), gluing and detecting properties of arrows

proof.text: Every local ring of $Z^+$ over $s_j$ is a local ring of $Y_j$ by Step 2, so is an integrally closed domain; over $U$ it is a local ring of the normal scheme $S$. Hence $Z^+$ is normal and reduced. Moreover each of its points over $s_j$ is a specialization of the generic point of $Y_j$, since $Y_j$ is integral; the localization projection takes that generic point to the common generic point over $U$. Points over $U$ are specializations of the same point because $S$ is integral. Thus every point of $Z^+$ is in the closure of that one generic point. It is nonempty, irreducible and reduced, hence integral. The maps $q$ and $b$ are isomorphisms over $U$, so $q$ induces the identity on the common function field.

source.place: Tag 0BFZ, identifying the glued normal modification; the argument uses the local-ring calculation of Step 2

proof.text: Identify $Z^+$ with the normalization of $W$ by an affine calculation. Since $q$ is integral, the inverse image of an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset W$ is affine $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ integral over $A$. Integrality of both schemes and the common function field embed $A\subseteq B\subseteq k(W)$. Normality makes $B$ integrally closed: an integral fraction belongs to every $B_{\mathfrak q}$ and hence to $B$; the last assertion follows since the ideal $\{d\in B:dx\in B\}$ is contained in no maximal ideal if $x\in B_{\mathfrak q}$ for all maximal $\mathfrak q$. Thus $B\subseteq\overline A$ by integrality, while every element of $\overline A$ is integral over $B$ and lies in $B$. Therefore $B=\overline A$. These equalities inside the same function field agree under restriction, and the definition of normalization identifies $q$ globally with $W^\nu\to W$. Consequently $a$ is exactly the normalized point blowup of $Z_k$ at $z$, and it is proper by Step 6.

source.place: Tags 035I and 035Q, integral birational characterization, with the integral-closure argument written out; def-sc-normalization

proof.text: Put $Z_{k+1}=Z^+$ and increase just $a_i$ by one. Properness of $Z^+\to Z_k$ and $Z_k\to S$ gives properness over $S$ by composition, and finite type over the Noetherian $S$ gives that $Z^+$ is Noetherian. It already has finite presentation by its gluing construction; Step 7 gives normality and integrality. The chosen local identifications and the lifted arrow $a$ show that its tower over $S_i$ has exactly the prescribed next step and its tower over every other $S_j$ has an identity step. All restrictions over $U$ are identities. This proves the induction invariant for $k+1$. At $k=N$, the interleaving has used every prescribed operation once, giving the required global tower and the endpoint identifications. Finally apply Step 2 to $X=Z_N$: every point over $s_i$ has the asserted unique corresponding point and local-ring isomorphism.
